verdicts.reason: Every quote verifies verbatim. 01.06.02-credit-backed-portfolio.md:63 and :211 state attester identity publishes 'Never, at any tier, to any viewer', and :117 spells out 'Not who.' Against that, 01.06.01-profile-page-composition.md:97 (Happy Path, normative narrative) says the Record shows 'what this person did on it and who said so'; 01.06.01:135 gives the ratified anti-laundering remedy as the string 'Tambourine — Song, attested by Sam Reeves'; and 01.06.03-epk-generation-sharing.md:42 (Happy Path) says the promoter 'can see who attested each one'. The 01.06.03 case is on an unauthenticated public surface. I searched the whole domain for 'supersed|stale|reconcil' — no marker, no superseding note, and no reconciliation entry in 01.06-portfolio-media-epk-cx.md (its CX-01/CX-02/CX-03 discuss the asserted/attested seam and never mention attester identity). The scope objection fails too: 01.06-portfolio-media-epk-cx.md:11 makes the portfolio 'the EPK's substance', so these are the same facts on three surfaces. Two normative statements that cannot both hold, on the domain's most-visited surface, with nothing tracking the divergence. Blocking upheld.

The quote at 01.05.02-claim-initiation-proof-methods.md:80 verifies, but it is misread as two independently-satisfiable grants. The row is a partition, and its right-hand cell already decides the band case: 'Grant a signing mandate **or add a member with one** (01.03) — a laundering route' is a flat prohibition on adding any member who arrives holding signing authority. Under 01.03.03-mandate-scope-delegated-authority.md:40 a confirmed `permanent` band member is exactly such a member, so permanent adds fall under the 'may not' column and touring/staff adds (01.03.03:42 — 'presence with zero authority') fall under the 'may'. Nothing is jointly unsatisfiable. The derivation is also stated as a rule rather than left to inference: 01.05.02:231 D-08 — 'Provisional control may do anything the platform can undo, and nothing it cannot ... A derivation rule, not a list — it stays correct as new domains land' — and 01.05.02:72 repeats it, which is precisely the instruction to re-derive against later-landing decisions like the DQ-02.4 seed. Both competent readings converge on: a provisional owner may not create a seeded permanent edge.

Quotes verify, but the owning file states the outcome for the non-monetary case explicitly rather than leaving it to invention. 01.03.03-mandate-scope-delegated-authority.md:48 is unconditional: 'The seed includes `administer`. Any confirmed permanent member can therefore alter another member's mandate, invite, and remove.' 01.03.03:55 (Happy Path step 3) says the drummer already holds all seven activities with nobody granting anything, and 01.03.03:69 accepts the consequence in terms — 'There is no pre-act gate below the ceiling; the defences are all after the fact.' A value ceiling denominated in money is not exceeded by an act carrying no monetary value; the escalation path at 01.03.03:64 is described as triggering when an 'Action exceeds the mandate's value ceiling', which an unvalued act cannot do. The claimed Implementer B reading (unvalued ⇒ unbounded ⇒ escalate to the creator alone) would directly contradict :48, :55 and 01.03.02-representation-roster-relationships.md:46 ('*any* `confirmed` `permanent` member can accept'), and would reinstate the creator-privilege asymmetry 01.03.03:40 explicitly refuses ('not a superior grade'). No competent reading lands there.

Quotes verify at all four sites. 01.01.03-acting-context-switcher.md:34 makes shared aliases a derivation source 'subject to 01.01.02 Q-01'; :123 prescribes a presence indicator for 'Two co-owners of a shared alias'; :167 (DT-10) and :179 both call the collision 'evidence for 01.01.02 Q-01'. 01.01.02-artist-names-aliases-projects.md:152 D-04 closes it in the opposite direction ('Aliases are single-owner by construction'), :165 strikes Q-01 through as RESOLVED, and :135 says in terms that 'CX-02's shared-alias race condition and its permission-intersection question both dissolve — two people can never act as one alias'. Both files carry Last updated 2026-07-23, so the propagation was one-sided; 01.01-person-identity-roles-cx.md:54 and :56 carry the same stale construct. No marker anywhere. This is a genuine unmarked internal contradiction and I uphold it. Downgraded from blocking to warning under rule 7: the residue is dead spec, not invented product behaviour — D-04 is unmissable, and both implementers ship single-owner aliases, one of them having also written an unreachable shared-alias branch. The 'treat alias ownership as undecided' instruction at :34 is the real cost, and it is a warning-grade one.

The premise that '01.03.03 defines no such role' is wrong on inspection. 01.03.03-mandate-scope-delegated-authority.md:25 names `administer` as one of the seven activities and 01.02.02 D-07 supplies the owning mandate — i.e. 01.03 supplies exactly the two things 'owner/admin' names, and 01.02.03-organization-type-transitions.md:51 uses that same pair in its user-facing copy ('Only an owner or admin of this entity can add a capability'). The band outcome the finding calls unresolved is ratified and disclosed: 01.03.03:48 — 'The seed includes `administer`. Any confirmed permanent member can therefore alter another member's mandate, invite, and remove' — with the file explicitly noting this is wider than the legal default and must be disclosed. 01.03-membership-representation-mandate-cx.md:35 repeats it. DT-04's rationale at 01.02.03:73 is satisfied on the same reading: a session player linked to a studio holds nothing, because 01.03.03:43 D-10 gives studios/venues/labels/shops/agencies no seed at all. Implementer B's owning-mandate-only reading requires discarding the '/admin' half of a term whose referent is defined in the cited file.

The quotes verify but the reconciliation the finding says was never performed is in meta/constraints.md itself, in the same table row the finding cites. constraints.md:267 reads: 'Consumer protection / returns | Physical + digital goods | **v1.5** | US has no federal 14-day withdrawal right (unlike EU) — returns are policy-driven per seller. Digital-goods no-refund is simpler in the US than the EU CRD path already specified in 14.09.01 (**keep that logic, gate it by jurisdiction**).' That is an explicit standing instruction to retain the EU-drafted consumer-protection logic and gate it, not to retire it — and it phases the whole surface to v1.5, so no v1 US listing flow is blocked by 01.08 D-04. The sibling-remediation argument also inverts: 01.02.01-organization-types-attributes.md:163 Q-03 states that the D-14 / D-72 place-record profile pattern explicitly does NOT reach this axis — 'the statutory returns floor is a property of the *buyer's* jurisdiction, not the record's address, so it does not resolve against the place-record regime profile D-14 uses' — and routes it to `/create-prd-security` with 13/14. 01.08:93 Q-02 tracks the same question from its own side, owner User, target `/create-prd-security`. 01.07 D-06 and 01.02.01 D-14 govern statutory *credential and venue* vocabularies (domain 16's regime axis), a different axis the tree names as different.

Quotes verify (01.03.01-membership-records-lifecycle.md:63 does open a '`permanent + staff (2028–)`' period). But the seed rule resolves it as written: 01.03.03-mandate-scope-delegated-authority.md:40 keys on an edge 'whose current capacity period is `permanent`', and a period of permanent+staff is permanent; :42 D-09 says 'The seed attaches to `permanent` only' — an exclusion of the three non-permanent capacities, not a purity test. 01.03.01:81's 'edges outside the peer seed' is scoped by its own scenario header ('Touring member who is not a real member') to edges whose capacity is touring/staff/honorary. The claimed Implementer B outcome — a founding member silently losing all band authority and their acting context by agreeing to run front-of-house — is contradicted by the Happy Path it occurs inside (:63 → :64 records the drummer acting normally until departure), and by 01.03-membership-representation-mandate-cx.md:36, which classifies silent authority change as a security-grade event nobody has decided to trigger. No competent implementer reaches it.

The stray value is real — 01.03.01-membership-records-lifecycle.md:82 does contain 'crew 2015–2017, staff 2017–2020, permanent 2020–' — but it sits inside a quoted illustrative display string in an Edge Case whose subject is capacity *versioning*, while the enum is stated normatively twice: :34 ('permanent / touring / staff / honorary, each with its own date range') and :162 D-03, the latter documenting a deliberate removal that marks the enum as closed and curated. That closure signal cuts against the finding rather than for it: no implementer widens an enum whose own decision record shows values being taken out, on the strength of one prose example. The example also loses nothing normative when mapped to the enum — a roadie and a sound engineer are both `staff` — so the canonical scenario ('roadie → sound engineer → member') remains representable as staff→permanent with the tenure unbroken, which is the only property D-10 is protecting. Nothing downstream (01.03.03 D-09's seed key, 01.01.03's context derivation, :111's lineup grouping) changes under that mapping.

The load-bearing half of the claim — that the deferral targets 'a stage that has already run for this sub-domain' — is false. 01.04.02-name-trademark-ownership.md:5 carries **Status: [SURFACE]**, 01.04-band-ensemble-governance-index.md:5 carries **Status: [BREADTH]**, and :21 lists 01.04.02 as `[SURFACE]` in the Children table. `/ideate-discover` Step 5 deepening has not run for this file, so `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` at :48 is a live deferral pointing at a stage that genuinely has not executed, in the tree's standard marker idiom. That the row's premise is now unreachable under 01.01.02 D-04 (2026-07-23) is expected of an un-deepened file last touched 2026-07-16 — reconciling it is exactly what the pending stage is for. The substantive rule the finding says is missing is also reachable and cross-linked: 01.01.02-artist-names-aliases-projects.md:134 states that governance capture fires from alias creation and from E-28 promotion and names 01.04 as the target, and :94 E-30 routes the co-owner fallout to 01.04.04 by name.

Verified on both sides. identity-profiles-organizations-index.md:78 gives Operator ❌ None for 01.04, while 01.04-band-ensemble-governance-index.md:35 and :37 give Operator 👁️ Read-only for 01.04.02 and 01.04.04, and both child Role Lenses state the grant and its purpose (01.04.02:17 — 'A venue that books "Wolf Alice" needs to know which party that name currently is'; 01.04.04:18 — 'whether this band can still be booked, and if the name has transferred, which party it now resolves to'). The 'access icons are shorthand' rule does not rescue this: ❌ None is an affirmative denial, not an omission of detail, and the index does not leave it as an icon — :88 reasons about this specific cell and justifies it as 'an Operator has no standing in a band they are not part of', a rationale that is factually wrong for both grants, which exist *only* for the non-member venue. That the same index reconciles the Fan column for 01.04 at :90 as 'load-bearing rather than incidental' shows roll-up is the intended convention here, so the Operator cell is an unreconciled omission rather than a deliberate one. Warning is the correct severity — no product behaviour must be invented, but the pipeline key file asserts the opposite of its children.

Quotes verify (01.06-portfolio-media-epk-cx.md:95 R-02 and :55 CX-02 note 5 both treat 01.06.03 Q-01 as live), but the tracking pointer is explicit and lands on an unmissable closure: 01.06.03-epk-generation-sharing.md:103 marks Q-01 '✅ RESOLVED (Step 5, D-05/DT-04): stay **live**, never snapshot', with :96 D-05 and :74 DT-04 ('❌ REJECTED') carrying it, and the Behavior section at :34 restating it as the feature's model. Anyone following the cx's own reference resolves the staleness in one hop. The claimed failure — an implementer building an opt-in snapshot mode — also requires reading R-02 as a grant, when it sits in a **Rejected Pairs** table and rejects snapshotting; its residual clause defers the narrow case rather than authorising anything. Both readings converge on a live view with a sender-side watch. Stale cx hygiene, not a divergence-producing tracking failure.
